front: Which LACP mode pairs form an EtherChannel?
back: active–active and active–passive. passive–passive never forms, because neither end starts negotiation.

front: One of two EtherChannel member links fails. What happens?
back: The port-channel stays up on the remaining link with half the capacity. A brief loss is possible.

front: SW1 has base STP priority 24576. What priority does it show for VLAN 20?
back: 24596: the base priority plus the VLAN ID.

front: A trunk drops VLAN 20 from its allowed list. What happens to the router's .20 subinterface?
back: It can stay up/up, because the physical link is still up. Check the allowed VLANs with show interfaces trunk.
On the router interface facing the clients, pointing at the DHCP server's address.

front: What does passive-interface do in OSPF?
back: Stops hellos, so no neighbor forms on that interface. Its connected network is still advertised.

front: What does default-information originate need before it advertises a default route?
back: A default route already in the router's own routing table, unless the always keyword is added.

front: An OSPF neighbor is FULL but a route is missing. What do you check?
back: That the missing network is enabled in OSPF on the far router, and that both ends use the same network type.

front: Which three things make interface PAT work?
back: ip nat inside and ip nat outside on the right interfaces, an ACL selecting inside sources, and ip nat inside source list … interface … overload.

front: Why can a router's own ping fail when its clients reach the Internet through PAT?
back: The ping leaves with the router's transit address, which the NAT ACL does not match. Source it from a LAN address.

front: What does an entry in show ip nat translations prove?
back: That an outbound packet was translated. It does not prove the reply came back.

front: Why must a guest ACL permit DHCP first, with source any?
back: A new client's Discover goes from 0.0.0.0 to 255.255.255.255, UDP 68 to 67, so a guest-subnet permit would not match it.

front: A stateless ACL denies guest-to-staff traffic. How can a staff ping to a guest still work?
back: Permit ICMP echo-reply from guest to staff above the deny. Each packet is still judged alone.

front: How do you restrict which source addresses can SSH to a device?
back: Apply a standard ACL to the VTY lines with access-class <name> in. An interface ACL filters transit traffic instead.

front: What does a device need before it accepts SSH with local accounts?
back: Hostname, domain name, RSA keys and a local username, then login local and transport input ssh on the VTY lines.
